title: 93-96% 'win rate' that was really a volatility counter
strategy: Nifty-100 option-buying edge scanner (5-min data, ADX filter)
headline: Scanner showed 92-96% win rate on Adani stocks, Eternal, Lodha
what_went_wrong: The scanner counted a 'win' as a 0.5% move within 12 candles. Direction, stop loss, option premium, theta and costs were not part of the definition, so the number measures how much a stock moves, not whether a trade makes money.
lesson: A win rate is only meaningful if it is measured on real trades with entry, stop, exit and costs. If a result looks above 80%, first suspect the definition.
status: Confirmed from your printed output; definition read from your own printed text

title: Same stocks, realistic trades: 35-38% win rate and negative expectancy
strategy: Volume-shock option-buying audit (1-min data, 15-min holding window)
headline: JIOFIN 35.0% win, expectancy -0.296%; COALINDIA 36.6% win, expectancy -0.368%
what_went_wrong: Once wins and losses were measured on actual entries and exits, the same kind of high-volatility stocks showed average losses (-1.9% to -2.3%) close to average wins (+2.2% to +3.1%) at a win rate well under 40%. That is a negative-expectancy system.
lesson: Put both numbers side by side: the flattering scan (entry 1) and the realistic audit (this entry). The realistic one is the one you can trade.

title: 1,764 trades, 32.6% win rate, but +117% average P&L per trade?
strategy: Fast/slow MA crossover on option candles with % stop and target
headline: Average PnL per trade 117.11% with a win rate of only 32.6%
what_went_wrong: An average gain above 100% per trade with a 1-in-3 win rate is not believable. Likely causes to check: very cheap, illiquid option candles producing huge percentage moves; entry at the option's close on the signal candle (look-ahead on a thin market); no costs or bid-ask spread; averaging percentages rather than rupees.
lesson: When one number looks impossible, stop and audit the data and units before looking at anything else. Report rupee P&L after costs next to percentage figures.
status: Needs your check: I read the code but did not re-run it, so the cause is a hypothesis

title: One trade was 54% of the total profit
strategy: 1-lakh capital option backtest using a delta proxy instead of real option prices
headline: Total P&L Rs 30,311; best single ADANIENSOL trade Rs 16,257; with the VEDL trade, two trades = 88%
what_went_wrong: Two winning trades produce nearly 88% of the profit; without them only about Rs 3,755 of the Rs 30,311 remains. Option P&L was also estimated from spot moves with a delta proxy, so theta, IV changes and bid-ask spread were not in the numbers.
lesson: Always check the profit with the top 1-2 trades removed. If the edge disappears, there was no edge, only luck.

title: One month supplied about half of a '4.7x in a year'
strategy: Apex Compounder V10, 5% risk per trade, H1 bars
headline: 372.93% ROI, 51 trades; September 2025 alone +119.39% (6 trades)
what_went_wrong: Equity went from 34,050 to 74,704 in one month (2.19x), which is about half of the total log-growth. The same 51 trades at lower risk (V8) returned 19.05%. The 372% is mostly position sizing applied to a handful of good trades, not a stronger edge. Your own note says to expect 30%+ drawdown at this risk level.
lesson: Compounding at high risk turns a small sample into a spectacular curve. Judge the signal at fixed small risk, and show the drawdown you would have lived through.

title: '559% return on deposit' is the same 51 trades, shown twice
headline: 559.43% return on deposit; max drawdown 23.88%, identical to the Apex run
what_went_wrong: The identical drawdown and trade count show this is the Apex trade list re-scaled to a $750 start, not independent evidence. Bonus-credit rules, lot-size rounding, spreads and slippage on a micro account are not modelled.
lesson: Re-scaling one backtest does not create a second backtest. Count each trade list once.

title: 100% win rate on 7 trades, labelled 'Validated & Optimized'
strategy: Signal audit, High vs Medium signals, 5-min tracking (10-19 Aug 2026)
headline: BANKNIFTY High signals 7/7 wins; 41 trades in the whole window; exits re-tuned on the same data
what_went_wrong: Seven wins out of seven only proves the true win rate is probably above about 65% (95% Wilson lower bound). Each cell has 6-9 trades over about eight trading days. The recommended exits (50 / 60-65 / 65-70 minutes) were read off the same data they were tested on.
lesson: Report a confidence range, not just a percentage. Fit exit rules on one period and test them on another that was never touched.

title: A hard-coded '58.9% win rate, profit factor 1.64' in the alert message
strategy: Multi-timeframe 50/200 EMA pullback signal bot (5-min, yfinance GC=F / BTC=F)
headline: Startup message claims a backtested win rate and profit factor; the script only downloads 5 days of data
what_went_wrong: The script itself can only see 5 days of 5-minute history, so the quoted statistics cannot come from it. A 240-period EMA on 5 days, continuous-futures roll gaps, and no stated costs also make the number fragile. Putting performance claims in messages that others may read can create compliance trouble.
lesson: Every performance figure should link to a saved run (data range, parameters, costs). Never type a number into an alert by hand.
status: Found in code review; the 58.9% / 1.64 figures themselves may come from a different test of yours

title: Stopped out in 1 minute: backtest vs live behaviour
strategy: Sniper V5 forward test: spot-based CE/PE signal, hard stop at signal-candle low
headline: VEDL CE entered at 324.00, hard stop at 322.75 hit after 1 minute; opposite PE signal 5 minutes later; both daily signals used by 15:07
what_went_wrong: The stop (about 0.4% away) sits inside normal 1-minute noise, and the signal came at 15:01, close to the end of the session. Whipsaw consumed both daily signals within about six minutes. Alerts are on the stock price, while the real option premium (spread, theta) moves differently.
lesson: Test stop distance against average candle range (ATR). Forward-test results are the honest check on a backtest; keep a log of every one.

title: Pairs bot: the profit-target exit can almost never fire
strategy: Titan V11 log-price regression pairs trade, window 168
headline: Z_EXIT = 0.0 with the exit test 'abs(z) <= Z_EXIT'
what_went_wrong: A float z-score is almost never exactly 0.0, so the take-profit exit does not trigger; the position would leave only through the z-stop (3.2) or the 10% capital stop. Mean-reversion strategies that never take profit end up as a series of stop-outs. The notebook also contains no historical backtest of this exact rule set.
lesson: Use a crossing test (sign change of z) or a small band such as 0.2, and unit-test exit conditions on synthetic data before going live.
status: Found in code review; please confirm against your live logs

title: Pairs bots: signal computed on a candle that has not closed
market: Crypto (SOL/LINK on Bybit demo and Delta)
strategy: Titan V1 / V6 / V11 z-score pair arbitrage
headline: Hourly bars polled every 5-10 seconds; z-score uses the still-forming latest bar
what_went_wrong: The latest row of the kline data is the open candle, so the z-score moves tick by tick and can cross the entry level and come back within the hour. That behaviour is not what a closed-bar backtest assumes. In V11 the ADF and Hurst filters are computed on the same 168-point window used to fit the hedge ratio, which makes them look better than they are. Across versions the leverage fell from 10x to 3x, and window, entry and filters were all changed, which suggests parameters were tuned after seeing results.
lesson: Decide on closed bars only, or backtest tick-level. Keep a record of each version's parameters and why they changed; a pile of tuned filters is a warning sign, not proof.

title: 'Asian box' sessions in broker time versus UTC
strategy: SMC liquidity-sweep bot on MT5 versus Pine strategy on TradingView
headline: MT5 bot defines the Asian range as broker hours 0-8; the Pine strategy uses 13:00-17:00 UTC
what_went_wrong: MT5 server time is usually offset from UTC and often shifts with daylight saving, so the 'Asian' box and the trading window may not mean the same hours across weeks or between platforms. Results from one tool will not match the other, and the difference is easy to miss.
lesson: Store all timestamps in UTC and convert only for display. When two platforms disagree, compare a single day trade by trade.
status: Needs your check: depends on your broker's server time zone
